newsitem.title: USA: Concerns about Dell Computer hit stock - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Concerns about Dell Computer hit stock - analyst.

text.p: Concerns about Dell Computer Corp.'s second-quarter earnings took the stock of the personal computer maker lower Tuesday, an analyst said.

Dell's second quarter is "not historically a strong one," unlike the first quarter when revenues were driven by government sales activity, a Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette analyst said in a note to clients.

"We spoke with management and found the company remains confident about the pace of business and is comfortable with (Wall) Street mean revenue estimates of $2.65 billion and $1.07 in earnings per share," said analyst Kevin McCarthy.
The note to clients was made available to Reuters Tuesday.
McCarthy said Dell's stock has fallen recently on concerns about the quarter, which ends July 31. Dell stock closed Tuesday down $3.0625 at $114.375 on Nasdaq.

"Some may interpret these comments as a change in the company's confidence level. We see them as fairly routine boilerplate caution," McCarthy wrote regarding the personal computer company's statements.
In the 1996 second quarter, Austin, Texas-based Dell earned $103 million, or $1.05 a share, on revenues of $1.69 billion.
A Dell spokesman said, "I think the most pertinent comment to focus on (by McCarthy) is that this is fairly routine boilerplate caution.

"In our first-quarter analysts' earnings call, we indicated in our outlook that the second quarter is typically one of the weaker quarters seasonally. Many U.S. governments come off peak buying in the first quarter because their fiscal year ended March 31," the Dell spokesman said.
